common_name: Allen's Cascadia Dahlia (White Laciniated Cactus Dahlia, ADS Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant tubers after soil has warmed and frost danger has passed; this medium-sized laciniated cactus type rewards full sun and even moisture with crisp white blooms.

directions: Set tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed, spacing plants to allow air circulation around the narrow, laciniated (split and twisted) white petals. Stake or cage plants early since medium-class laciniated blooms can be heavy on the stem. This cultivar, bred by Allen Manuel, earned the American Dahlia Society's Derrill W. Hart Medal in 2023 as a standout new seedling. Deadhead spent blooms regularly to extend the late-summer flowering display.

common_name: LLW Sunrise Dahlia (Light Yellow-Pink Blend Semi-Cactus Dahlia, ADS Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant once nighttime temperatures stay reliably above 50F; small semi-cactus blooms hold their soft yellow-and-pink blend color best with some afternoon shade in hot climates.

directions: This compact semi-cactus dahlia produces small blooms blending light yellow and pink tones, with petals that curve back softly rather than rolling into tight cactus quills. Bred by Lisa Walny, it was recognized with the American Dahlia Society's Derrill W. Hart Medal in 2023, an award given to promising newly introduced seedlings. Pinch the central growing tip early to encourage branching and a fuller display of flowers. Regular feeding during bud set improves both bloom count and color saturation.

common_name: Skipley Road Sherry Dahlia (Red Miniature Formal Decorative Dahlia, ADS Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant in full sun after frost danger passes; the tightly ranked, symmetrical red petals of this miniature formal decorative type make it a strong cut-flower candidate.

directions: Skipley Road Sherry carries saturated red miniature blooms with the neat, evenly overlapping petal rows typical of the formal decorative class. Bred by Richard Williams, it received the American Dahlia Society's Derrill W. Hart Medal in 2023 for its exhibition-quality form. Disbud side shoots to concentrate energy into fewer, larger show-quality flowers. Consistent watering through summer heat helps keep petal color from fading.

common_name: Irish Moon Dahlia (Yellow Miniature Ball Dahlia, ADS Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant tubers in rich, well-drained soil after frost; the tightly rolled, spherical yellow blooms of this miniature ball type are a reliable long-season bloomer.

directions: Irish Moon forms clean, globe-shaped golden-yellow blooms in the miniature ball class, with petals spiraling tightly from base to tip. Bred by Sandy and Steve Boley, it was honored with the American Dahlia Society's Derrill W. Hart Medal in 2023. The compact, bushy habit suits containers as well as cutting gardens. Stake lightly in windy sites since ball dahlias can topple under their own bloom weight.

common_name: Sandia Ruthie Dahlia (Dark Pink Stellar Dahlia, ADS Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant once soil is reliably warm; the airy, narrow-petaled stellar form of this dark pink cultivar produces an abundance of elegant sprays well suited to bouquets.

directions: Sandia Ruthie belongs to the stellar class, prized for slim, slightly twisted dark pink petals that give the bloom a starburst outline rather than a dense, rounded profile. Bred by Sandy and Steve Boley, it earned the American Dahlia Society's Derrill W. Hart Medal in 2023. Its naturally branching habit yields many long-stemmed flowers over an extended season, making it a favorite for cutting. Light, regular feeding keeps stems strong enough to support the open, airy blooms.

common_name: Clearview Ginger Dahlia (Dark Pink Miniature Dahlia, ADS Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant in full sun with excellent drainage; the dark pink miniature blooms of this cultivar show best with a bit of afternoon relief from intense heat.

directions: Bred by Richard Parshall of the Clearview Dahlias breeding program, this miniature cultivar carries deep pink blooms. It was awarded the American Dahlia Society's Lynn B. Dudley Medal in 2023 for its outstanding seedling bench scores across member shows nationwide. The tidy plant habit makes it a strong candidate for show benches and small garden beds alike. Remove the first terminal bud to encourage a fuller flush of side blooms.

common_name: Narrows Lilly Dahlia (Dark Pink Semi-Cactus Dahlia, ADS Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant after frost danger has passed, giving the plant rich, moisture-retentive soil to support its vigorous deep pink semi-cactus flowers.

directions: Narrows Lilly was bred by Ken and Marilyn Walton and carries rich dark pink blooms with the loosely curved, semi-recurved petals characteristic of the semi-cactus form. It was recognized with the American Dahlia Society's Lynn B. Dudley Medal in 2023, reflecting consistently strong scores on seedling evaluation benches. The plant branches freely, giving a steady succession of flowers through late summer into fall. Mulching around the base helps conserve soil moisture during peak bloom.

common_name: 20th Ave for Mom Dahlia (Dark Pink Miniature Ball Dahlia, ADS Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant in full sun after soil has warmed; the dense, perfectly rounded dark pink blooms of this miniature ball type benefit from even watering to avoid bud drop.

directions: Bred by Rich Gibson, this sentimentally named miniature ball dahlia produces densely packed, spiraled dark pink flowers on a compact, floriferous plant. It received the American Dahlia Society's Lynn B. Dudley Medal in 2023 after earning top marks across multiple regional seedling benches. Its sturdy stems and uniform bloom shape make it a dependable choice for both garden display and cut-flower arrangements. Deadhead consistently to keep new buds forming through the season.

common_name: SB's Star Dahlia (Dark Red Orchid-Form Dahlia, ADS Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant in full sun once nights stay warm; the open, narrow-petaled orchid form of this dark red cultivar displays best with good airflow between plants.

directions: Bred by Sandy and Steve Boley, SB's Star shows deep velvety red petals arranged in the open, single-whorled, pointed-ray pattern of the orchid-flowered dahlia class. It earned the American Dahlia Society's Evie Gullikson Medal in 2023, an award honoring outstanding new seedlings from the show circuit. The airy flower form contrasts well against denser decorative and ball types in mixed plantings. Regular deadheading keeps the plant producing fresh blooms into autumn.

common_name: Lo-Peach Dahlia (Dark Blend Mignon Single Dahlia, ADS Award Winner)

planting.note: Plant after frost risk passes; this mignon single cultivar's smoky dark-blend petal coloring deepens with cooler autumn temperatures.

directions: Bred by Wayne Lobaugh, Lo-Peach is a mignon single dahlia with warm, smoky dark-blend coloring that shifts subtly between bronze and peach tones depending on light and temperature. It was honored with the American Dahlia Society's Evie Gullikson Medal in 2023 for its strong, consistent performance on seedling evaluation benches. The plant's compact habit keeps it tidy in small garden spaces or large containers. Consistent moisture through bud set helps the unusual coloring develop fully.

common_name: KA's Khaleesi Dahlia (White Informal Decorative Dahlia, ADS Stanley Johnson Medal Winner)

planting.note: Plant in full sun after soil has warmed; this award-winning white informal decorative dahlia needs sturdy staking to support its large, exhibition-caliber blooms.

directions: Bred by Kristine Albrecht of Santa Cruz Dahlias under her KA's dahlia line, this crisp white informal decorative cultivar carries loosely twisted petals in a full, substantial bloom. It won the American Dahlia Society's Stanley Johnson Medal in 2023, the Society's top honor recognizing the single best new seedling of the year across the national show circuit. Give plants generous spacing and early staking, since the large flowers can weigh down stems in wind or rain. Regular disbudding channels energy into fewer, show-quality blooms.

common_name: Clearview Citron Dahlia (Lemon-Ice Yellow Incurved Cactus Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant in full sun with well-drained soil; the clear lemon-ice yellow, inward-curving petals of this small incurved cactus type keep their crisp color through the heat of summer.

directions: Introduced by Dick and Danielle Parshall's Clearview Dahlias breeding program, Clearview Citron produces bright, clean lemon-ice yellow blooms in the small incurved cactus class, with petal tips rolling inward toward the center. Though Clearview Dahlias itself ceased operating in the years after Danielle Parshall's death, this cultivar remains in commerce through other dahlia growers. The compact plant habit suits garden borders as well as cut-flower rows. Pinch young plants to encourage branching and a longer run of blooms through late summer.

common_name: Clearview Royal Dahlia (Dark Blend Miniature Ball Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant once soil has warmed; the tightly spiraled, deep-toned blend coloring of this miniature ball type is a reliable, long-blooming garden performer.

directions: Introduced by the Clearview Dahlias breeding program, Clearview Royal forms small, perfectly spherical blooms in a rich dark color blend, with petals spiraling tightly from the outer edge to the center. The plant stays compact and floriferous, producing a steady supply of flowers well suited to cutting. Stake lightly in exposed sites since the dense ball-shaped blooms can be heavy relative to the stem. Deadhead regularly to keep new buds forming through the fall.

common_name: Clearview Blaze Dahlia (Flame Blend Miniature Formal Decorative Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant in full sun after frost danger passes; the warm red-orange-yellow flame blend coloring of this miniature formal decorative type is most vivid in cooler fall weather.

directions: Clearview Blaze, introduced by Dick and Danielle Parshall around 2000, carries miniature formal decorative blooms blending red, orange, and yellow into a fiery flame pattern across each neatly ranked petal. The symmetrical form makes it a strong candidate for exhibition as well as garden color. Disbud competing side shoots early if larger, show-quality blooms are desired. Even moisture and regular feeding help intensify the blended coloring as temperatures cool in late summer.

common_name: Clearview Jonas Dahlia (Light Blend Large Semi-Cactus Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant in rich, well-drained soil after frost danger passes; the large, loosely curved yellow-and-pink blend blooms of this semi-cactus type need sturdy staking.

directions: Introduced by the Clearview Dahlias breeding program, Clearview Jonas produces large semi-cactus blooms blending soft yellow and pink tones, with petals curving gently rather than rolling into tight quills. Its substantial flower size calls for early staking and generous spacing to let the plant reach full size without crowding. Feed consistently through the growing season to support the large blooms, and deadhead to keep new flowers coming through autumn.
